DoodleSite sketch to prototype

A presentation of the system: what it is, the files that define it, and a recorded walkthrough.

OverviewWhat the system is BlueprintEvery file, with a plain-English pane Usage guideA recorded session, step by step
Evidence
6 scenarios through the real pipeline, every check passing, 18 min of generation.
Scenario gallery (all generated designs) Download the blueprint (.zip) GitHub (private)

Draw where things go. Say what it is. Get a page that shows its reading.

A rough doodle carries what a text prompt cannot: where things sit, how big they are, the order they read in. A one-line brief carries what a sketch cannot. DoodleSite sends both to Claude, through an API key or the Claude Code CLI already on the machine, and gets back a self-contained page plus the model's own account of every mark.

See the recorded walkthrough Read the blueprint Download the blueprint (.zip)

The north star

Nothing is generated silently. The sketch decides placement, the brief decides meaning, and the model must account for every mark: each one becomes a row in the reading, each guess an entry under "unclear", each motion instruction a listed trigger. If the account is wrong, the fix is a rule in a Markdown module, and the scenario suite says whether the rule worked.

How it works, four steps

Two inputs, one model call, two outputs every time: the page and the reading.

1Sketch

Boxes, lines, crossed boxes, circles, arrows, red notes, or a photo of paper that is cleaned up on the way in.

doodle.png

2Brief

One line or a paragraph. Wins over the sketch where they disagree; the sketch decides placement where it is silent.

brief text

3Build

The prompt is assembled from the modules this request needs and sent with the image to the chosen back-end. Output streams in with markers.

<<<HTML>>> document

4Read and refine

Regions, unclear marks, motion, assumptions, changes. Every build is a version; the next brief is a delta on any of them.

analysis JSON

The data flow

  1. Sheet to PNG1200 by 800 or 800 by 1200, white, grid stripped. A dropped photo is flattened first: shadows out, paper white, red notes still red.
  2. Prompt assemblycore + rough + motion, then create or adjust, then refine if there is a previous result, then the output contract. Cached per shape.
  3. ProviderAPI: image block plus cached system prompt, streamed. CLI: image on disk, prompt from a file, Read tool only, stream-json.
  4. Marked output<<<ANALYSIS>>> JSON, <<<HTML>>> document, <<<END>>>. Parsed while partial so the preview renders mid-stream.
  5. Preview and readingSandboxed iframe at phone, tablet, or full width; the reading tab shows the analysis as tables.
  6. VersionsKept in the browser, twenty deep. Refine from any one; the model lists what it changed.

One pipeline, two back-ends

ANTHROPIC_API_KEYAnthropic APIclaude-opus-5 by default, adaptive thinking, the system prompt cached. Streams up to 64,000 tokens.
claude on PATHLocal Claude CodeThe CLI you are already logged into, in print mode with the tools limited to Read. No key, no extra cost line.

Auto mode picks the API when a key exists and the CLI otherwise. The settings drawer overrides either per browser. This presentation's runs used the CLI with claude-fable-5-1.

Exposed three ways

  • Web app sketch, brief, build, read, refine; adjust an existing site by URL or pasted markup.
  • Scenario runner node scenarios/run.mjs sends hand-drawn wireframes through the real pipeline and checks the results.
  • Project skills three Claude Code skills so changing a rule, adding a scenario, or restyling the UI follows the same method every time.

Blueprint 20 files

The real files that define the system. The centre pane shows the file as it is in the repository; the right pane says what it is for and what to remember.

Usage guide

A real session recorded with Playwright: a landing page for a small hiking-tour company, drawn, briefed, built through the local Claude Code CLI, and toured. The wait for the model is played at 14x; nothing else is edited.

Step by step

The same session as still frames, with what is happening at each point.

1Open the workbench

A gridded sheet on the left, the result pane on the right. The pill in the corner says which back-end will answer: here, the local Claude Code CLI, found and logged in. The grid is for you; it is never sent.

2Draw the layout

Boxes for components, a word inside to name them, lines for text, a crossed box for a photo. The red ink is a note to the model and will not appear on the page. Keys: P pen, M marker, B box, T text, E eraser.

3Write a one-line brief

What it is, who it is for, what the three cards are. The brief wins where it disagrees with the sketch; the sketch decides placement where the brief is silent.

4Build

The sheet is exported as a plain PNG, the prompt is assembled from the modules this request needs, and the request goes to the chosen back-end. A pencil line draws across the result pane while it works.

5Watch the page arrive

The code view fills as the model writes. The preview renders as soon as a body exists. The status line says what is happening; Stop aborts the provider.

6See the result

The page lands as version 1, with the model and token usage under the actions. Copy the code, download the HTML, or open it in its own tab.

7Check it at phone width

The same document in a 390px frame. The prompt asks for responsiveness down to 360px and the scenario checks enforce a viewport meta.

8Read how it read you

Mark by mark: what was drawn, where it sat, what it became, the gaps it filled, the marks it was unsure about, and any motion instructions it found.

9Refine in rounds

Write the next brief and refine from any version. The model applies it as a delta to the previous result and lists exactly what it changed.

One worked example

Rough ballpoint sketch, photographed: Open boxes, a struck-out element, half-legible labels, a crease, a stain, and uneven light, plus motion marks: a slide-in arrow, a fade label, a hover note, and a scroll reveal. Brief: "Spoke & Chain, a bike repair workshop in Leeds. One page."

What the model said it saw

The sketch is a one-page bike workshop site: a logo-and-name nav with Services / Book / Find us, a hero with a large bike photo on the left that slides in and heading, copy and a 'book now' button on the right that fade in, a row of three service cards that reveal on scroll, and a footer with hours, phone and a map. Built as a bold, hi-vis-and-ink workshop page for Spoke & Chain in Leeds.

DrawnWhereBuilt asNotes
circle + 'spoke & chain', 'services book find us'top full-width barHeader with chainring logo mark, brand name and three anchor links (#services, #book, #find-us)Nav wraps on narrow screens; brand stays left, links right.
large box with X, 'bike pic'hero, left ~55%Tinted image placeholder with an inline SVG bicycle and a caption describing the intended photoThick ink border and hard yellow offset shadow carry the 'bold workshop feel' note.
thick line + several thin lineshero, right columnLarge condensed heading, a two-sentence intro and a short opening-hours lineHeading sized to match the thicker stroke in the sketch.
'book now' rounded boxhero right, under the textPrimary button 'Book now' linking to #bookHard-shadow yellow button; lifts on hover.
scribbled-out box right of the buttonhero rightOmittedRead as a deleted secondary button.
'services x3 ?' + three boxes with linesfull-width band below hero, three equal columnsServices section with three cards: Services & tune-ups, Wheels & brakes, Rebuilds & custom builds, each with a short description and from-priceCards use a yellow top rule and 1px border rather than drop shadows; stack to one column under 760px.
'hours / phone / map?'bottom full-widthFooter (#find-us) with three columns: opening hours, phone/booking contact (#book), and a stylised SVG map with addressDark ink background to bookend the page.

Marks it was not sure about

MarkWent withCould also be
'hover → lift' with a line towards the scribbled-out box beside 'book now'Applied the hover lift to the Book now button, the nearest surviving elementCould have been meant for the service cards; easy to move the .lift class to .card
'services x3 ?'Three service cardsThe ? may have questioned the count; four would also fit the grid
'map?' in the footerIncluded a stylised inline SVG map with a pin and the addressCould have been left as a text address with a 'Get directions' link only
'book' nav link with no booking section drawnBoth 'Book' and 'Book now' go to the booking/phone block in the footer (#book)A tel: link or a separate booking form section

Motion it found

ElementTriggerEffectDuration
Hero bike imageloadSlides in from the left while fading up to full opacity600ms ease-out
Hero heading, paragraph, hours line and Book now buttonloadFade in one after another, starting after the image arrives500ms each, 90ms stagger, 250ms initial delay
Book now buttonhoverLifts up-left 2px and its hard shadow grows180ms
Service cardsscrollFade up 24px into place when the row enters the viewport, staggered left to right500ms, 100ms stagger

Checks 20/20

  • ✓Complete HTML document
  • ✓Has a <title>
  • ✓Viewport meta present
  • ✓No lorem ipsum
  • ✓Every in-page link resolves
  • ✓No external scripts
  • ✓No hotlinked images
  • ✓Motion respects reduced-motion
  • ✓Scroll-reveal content is not hidden without a ready class
  • ✓Analysis reports motion and unclear lists
  • ✓Names the shop
  • ✓Three service cards (uneven boxes, 'x3')
  • ✓Scribbled-out second button recognised as deleted
  • ✓Only one hero button
  • ✓Four motion instructions found
  • ✓Hero entrance implemented
  • ✓Hover lift on the button
  • ✓Scroll reveal implemented
  • ✓Unclear marks reported
  • ✓Red margin note kept off the page

<style>
  :root {
    --ink: #141518;
    --steel: #2b3a42;
    --grey: #6b7378;
    --paper: #f1f2ee;
    --white: #ffffff;
    --yellow: #ffd23f;
    --max: 1180px;
    --pad: clamp(16px, 4vw, 40px);
  }

  * { box-sizing: border-box; }
  html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }
  body {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: "Barlow", system-ui, sans-serif;
    font-size: 17px;
    line-height: 1.55;
    color: var(--ink);
    background: var(--paper);
  }
  h1, h2, h3 {
    font-family: "Barlow Condensed", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif;
    font-weight: 800;
    line-height: 0.95;
    letter-spacing: 0.005em;
    margin: 0;
    text-transform: uppercase;
  }
  p { margin: 0; }
  a { color: inherit; }
  :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--yellow); outline-offset: 3px; }
  .wrap { max-width: var(--max); margin: 0 auto; padding-inline: var(--pad); }

  .skip {
    position: absolute; left: 12px; top: -60px;
    background: var(--ink); color: var(--yellow);
    padding: 10px 14px; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; z-index: 100;
  }
  .skip:focus { top: 12px; }

  /* ---------- Header ---------- */
  .site-header {
    background: var(--white);
    border-bottom: 3px solid var(--ink);
    position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 50;
  }
  .site-header .wrap {
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between;
    gap: 16px 24px; flex-wrap: wrap; min-height: 70px; padding-block: 10px;
  }
  .brand {
    display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px;
    text-decoration: none; font-family: "Barlow Condensed", sans-serif;
    font-weight: 800; font-size: 26px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em;
  }
  .brand svg { width: 40px; height: 40px; flex: none; }
  .nav { display: flex; gap: 6px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
  .nav a {
    display: inline-block; padding: 8px 12px; text-decoration: none;
    font-weight: 600; font-size: 16px; border-bottom: 3px solid transparent;
    transition: border-color 150ms;
  }
  .nav a:hover { border-bottom-color: var(--yellow); }

  /* ---------- Hero ---------- */
  .hero { padding-block: clamp(36px, 7vw, 88px); overflow: hidden; }
  .hero .wrap {
    display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.2fr) minmax(0, 1fr);
    gap: clamp(28px, 5vw, 64px); align-items: center;
  }
  .hero-media { margin: 0; position: relative; }
  .photo {
    background: var(--steel);
    border: 4px solid var(--ink);
    box-shadow: 14px 14px 0 var(--yellow);
    aspect-ratio: 4 / 3;
    display: grid; place-items: center;
    padding: 8%;
    position: relative;
  }
  .photo svg { width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
  .photo-cap {
    position: absolute; left: 0; bottom: 0; right: 0;
    background: rgba(20,21,24,0.78); color: var(--paper);
    font-size: 13px; padding: 8px 12px; letter-spacing: 0.01em;
  }
  .hero-copy h1 {
    font-size: clamp(48px, 7.2vw, 96px);
  }
  .hero-copy h1 mark {
    background: none; color: inherit;
    box-shadow: inset 0 -0.32em 0 var(--yellow);
  }
  .hero-copy .lede { margin-top: 22px; font-size: clamp(17px, 1.6vw, 20px); max-width: 44ch; }
  .hero-copy .open { margin-top: 14px; color: var(--steel); font-weight: 600; }
  .btn {
    display: inline-block; margin-top: 28px;
    background: var(--yellow); color: var(--ink);
    font-family: "Barlow Condensed", sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 22px;
    text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-decoration: none;
    padding: 14px 30px; border: 3px solid var(--ink);
    box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--ink);
    transition: transform 180ms ease, box-shadow 180ms ease;
  }
  .btn:hover, .btn:focus-visible { transform: translate(-2px, -2px); box-shadow: 7px 7px 0 var(--ink); }
  .btn:active { transform: translate(1px, 1px); box-shadow: 2px 2px 0 var(--ink); }

  /* ---------- Services ---------- */
  .services { padding-block: clamp(40px, 7vw, 88px); background: var(--white); border-top: 3px solid var(--ink); }
  .section-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 20px 32px; flex-wrap: wrap; margin-bottom: 32px; }
  .section-head h2 { font-size: clamp(38px, 5vw, 64px); }
  .section-head p { color: var(--grey); max-width: 48ch; }
  .cards { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 24px; }
  .card {
    background: var(--paper);
    border: 2px solid var(--ink);
    border-top: 10px solid var(--yellow);
    padding: 26px 24px 24px;
    display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px;
  }
  .card h3 { font-size: 30px; }
  .card p { color: var(--steel); }
  .card ul { margin: 4px 0 0; padding-left: 18px; color: var(--steel); }
  .card li { margin-bottom: 4px; }
  .price {
    margin-top: auto; padding-top: 14px; border-top: 1px dashed var(--grey);

  .price small { font-family: "Barlow", sans-serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 14px; color: var(--grey); }

  /* ---------- Footer / find us ---------- */
  .site-footer { background: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); padding-block: clamp(40px, 7vw, 80px) 32px; }
  .site-footer h2 { font-size: clamp(38px, 5vw, 64px); color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 28px; }
  .find { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1.3fr; gap: 32px; }
  .find h3 { font-size: 24px; color: var(--yellow); margin-bottom: 12px; }
  .hours { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; }
  .hours td { padding: 6px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(241,242,238,0.15); }
  .hours td:last-child { text-align: right; font-weight: 600; }
  .find a { color: var(--white); }
  .tel {
    display: block; font-family: "Barlow Condensed", sans-serif; font-weight: 800;
    font-size: 34px; text-decoration: none; letter-spacing: 0.02em; margin: 2px 0 8px;
  }
  .find .note { color: rgba(241,242,238,0.75); font-size: 15px; margin-top: 10px; }
  .map { border: 3px solid var(--paper); background: var(--steel); display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; }
  .addr { font-style: normal; margin-top: 12px; }
  .legal {
    margin-top: 48px; padding-top: 18px; border-top: 1px solid rgba(241,242,238,0.2);
    display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; flex-wrap: wrap;
    font-size: 14px; color: rgba(241,242,238,0.65);
  }

  /* ---------- Responsive ---------- */
  @media (max-width: 860px) {
    .hero .wrap { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
    .photo { box-shadow: 10px 10px 0 var(--yellow); }
    .find { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }
    .find > :last-child { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
  }
  @media (max-width: 760px) {
    .cards { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
  }
  @media (max-width: 520px) {
    .find { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
    .brand { font-size: 22px; }
    .nav a { padding: 8px 9px; font-size: 15px; }
  }

  /* ---------- Motion (only once JS is ready, only if the user allows it) ---------- */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
    .ready .hero-media { animation: slide-in 600ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1) both; }
    .ready .hero-copy > * { animation: fade-in 500ms ease-out both; animation-delay: 250ms; }
    .ready .hero-copy > :nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 340ms; }
    .ready .hero-copy > :nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 430ms; }
    .ready .hero-copy > :nth-child(4) { animation-delay: 520ms; }
    .ready .reveal { transition: opacity 500ms ease-out, transform 500ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1); }
    .ready .reveal:not(.in) { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(24px); }
    .ready .reveal:nth-child(2) { transition-delay: 100ms; }
    .ready .reveal:nth-child(3) { transition-delay: 200ms; }
    @keyframes slide-in {
      from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(-48px); }
      to   { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
    }
    @keyframes fade-in {
      from { opacity: 0; }
      to   { opacity: 1; }
    }
  }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    html { scroll-behavior: auto; }
    .btn, .nav a { transition: none; }
  }

<script>
  (function () {
    document.documentElement.classList.add('ready');
    var items = document.querySelectorAll('.reveal');
    if ('IntersectionObserver' in window) {
      var io = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
        entries.forEach(function (entry) {
          if (entry.isIntersecting) {
            entry.target.classList.add('in');
            io.unobserve(entry.target);
          }
        });
      }, { threshold: 0.2 });
      items.forEach(function (el) { io.observe(el); });
    } else {
      items.forEach(function (el) { el.classList.add('in'); });
    }
  })();
</script>

The scenario suite

Every sketch is SVG in a handwriting face, rendered to PNG, so each mark is reproducible. Runs go through the real pipeline and are checked automatically. The full set of generated pages is in the scenario gallery.
